newsitem.title: USA: S. Carolina House approves local option sales tax.
newsitem.headline: S. Carolina House approves local option sales tax.

text.p: The South Carolina House easily approved a bill allowing local governments to levy sales taxes for infrastructure projects, the State newspaper said Wednesday.
The proposal passed 104-11 and would require voter approval to levy the tax for up to seven years.
The bill now goes to the Senate.

Opponents said it would open the door for more than $500 million of new taxes. The House added several restrictions aimed at preventing that, including a ban on any local taxes not specifically authorized by the General Assembly.

They also required that a majority of the locally elected council approve tax increase, not just a majority of those present for the vote. The proposal would also cap local hotel bed taxes at three percent and meal and beverages taxes at two percent.

Local taxation has been a thorny issue for the legislature since 1995, when the state Supreme Court ruled that local governments could tax hotel beds and food and beverages to pay debt service on bond-financed projects. Some lawmakers feared the ruling could be interpreted to allow local governments to levy any kind of tax they want.
